title: John Lennon settles Big Seven Music Corp legal dispute | 1973
content:
John Lennon’s lawsuit with Big Seven Music Corp was formally settled on 12 October 1973.

The case, Big Seven Music Corp v Maclen Music Inc, Northern Songs Ltd, and Apple Records Inc, was brought in response to the similarity between The Beatles’ ‘Come Together’ and Chuck Berry’s ‘You Can’t Catch Me’. It had been settled out of court, but on this date the agreement was finalised in the United States District Court in New York City, in a hearing presided by Judge Thomas L Griesa.

John Lennon agrees to record three songs belonging to Big Seven publishers on his next album. The songs which John Lennon intends to record at this time are ‘You Can’t Catch Me’, ‘Angel Baby’ and ‘Ya Ya’. John Lennon reserves the right to alter the last two songs, that is, ‘Angel Baby’ and ‘Ya Ya’, to any title belonging to Big Seven but will in all events record ‘You Can’t Catch Me’.

John Lennon will use his best efforts to cause Apple to license to Big Seven, three songs from the Apple non-Beatle catalog, currently in circulation, excluding only those songs composed by John Lennon and Yoko Ono together and those composed by Paul McCartney and Linda McCartney together, to the extent that any of those songs can be in any manner considered to be an Apple non-Beatle product. In the alternative, if Apple for any reason does not license three songs to Big Seven prior to December 31, 1974, John Lennon agrees that he will record an additional two songs belonging to Big Seven, one song to be recorded prior to December 31, 1974 and one song prior to December 31, 1975.

At any time Mr. Lennon can choose the second alternative of recording two additional songs belonging to Big Seven, and is not obligated to pursue his undertaking to cause Apple to make the songs available, the three songs available to Big Seven if he makes such a selection.”

Rory Gallagher
Hot Press, July 1995
